construct: GBA1 encodes lysosomal acid beta-glucosidase (glucocerebrosidase), which hydrolyzes glucosylceramide into glucose and ceramide. Deficient activity causes accumulation of glucosylceramide and related lipids, especially in monocyte/macrophage-lineage cells, producing hepatosplenomegaly, cytopenias, bone disease, and characteristic Gaucher cells.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Massive splenomegaly, cytopenias, bone crises, Ashkenazi ancestry, and crumpled-paper macrophages indicate Gaucher disease due to GBA1/glucocerebrosidase deficiency with glucosylceramide storage.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Other sphingolipidoses can cause organomegaly and storage macrophages, but their substrates and histologic/clinical patterns differ; none matches classic Gaucher cells and bone crises.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The phenotype and macrophage morphology make glucosylceramide the uniquely supported stored substrate.
